questions.prompt: A 5 kg robot with two driven wheels of radius 0.04 m, rolling-resistance coefficient 0.02, climbs a 6 degree ramp at constant speed. Torque per wheel in N m. Precision 0.003.
A gearmotor datasheet lists a recommended continuous load of 15 kg cm. Convert it to N m (1 kg cm = 0.0980665 N m). Precision 0.01.
A 0.5 kg gripper and payload is held 0.4 m from a horizontal shoulder axis (the arm itself is ignored). Gravity torque in N m. Precision 0.01.
A 0.8 m move with a speed limit of 0.5 m/s and an acceleration limit of 1.0 m/s^2 uses a trapezoidal profile. Total time in seconds. Precision 0.02.
A 0.2 m move has a speed limit of 0.5 m/s and an acceleration limit of 1.0 m/s^2. The speed limit is never reached. Peak speed in m/s. Precision 0.005.
questions.explanation: v^2/a = 0.25 is at least 0.2, so the profile is a triangle with peak speed sqrt(d a) = sqrt(0.2) = 0.447 m/s.

questions.prompt: A load inertia of 20 kg cm^2 is driven by a motor with rotor inertia 0.1 kg cm^2. Smallest gear ratio that gives an inertia ratio of 10. Precision 0.02.
One cycle: 1.2 N m for 0.2 s, 0.4 N m for 1.6 s, 0.2 N m for 0.2 s, then rest at 0 for 2.0 s. RMS torque in N m. Precision 0.005.
A motor with R = 2.2 ohm and k_e = 0.011 V s/rad draws 1.0 A at a motor speed of 500 rad/s. The battery has sagged to 10 V. PWM duty needed as a fraction. Precision 0.01.
A square-thread screw has lead 5 mm, mean diameter 12 mm and friction coefficient 0.15. Efficiency when raising a load (a fraction). Precision 0.01.
A designer doubles the gear ratio of a joint. What happens to the load inertia seen at the motor shaft?
options: It halves.
It falls by a factor of 4.
It doubles.
It does not change.
questions.explanation: Reflected load inertia is J_L / i^2, so doubling i divides it by 4 (Parker: reduced by 1/ratio^2).

questions.prompt: Why should you not size a joint from the stall torque in a datasheet?
options: Because stall torque is always below the working torque.
Because it is the extrapolated extreme of the speed-torque line, and real performance is closer to the measured performance graph.
Because stall torque only applies at 25 degrees C ambient.
Because stall torque is measured with the gearbox removed.
questions.explanation: Stall torque is the maximum momentary torque at zero speed, quoted for comparison. The ROBOTIS e-manual states that real performance is generally closer to the performance graph, and Pololu notes that units stall well before the extrapolated point.

questions.prompt: A steep, multi-start lead screw is fast and efficient. What must you plan for on a vertical axis?
options: Nothing: all lead screws hold their load when the power is off.
It is probably not self-locking, so the load can back-drive it; add a brake, counterweight or spring.
The screw becomes self-locking at high speed.
The motor must run at a lower voltage.
questions.explanation: Self-locking needs mu sec(alpha) at least tan(lead angle). A steep lead has a large tan(lambda), so efficiency is high but the screw back-drives. Even self-locking screws can creep under vibration (Wikipedia, Leadscrew).

questions.prompt: A motor's peak torque requirement is within its peak rating, but the motor overheats in a repeating cycle. What was probably checked wrongly?
options: The PWM frequency.
The RMS torque over the cycle against the continuous (rated) torque.
The encoder resolution.
The motor colour code.
questions.explanation: Peak torque limits short bursts; heat follows the RMS current over the cycle. A design can pass the peak check and still overheat if T_rms exceeds the rated torque.

questions.prompt: A stepper's pull-out curve in its datasheet was measured at 24 V. You plan to run it from 12 V. What can you conclude?
options: The same torque is available at every speed.
The torque at speed will probably be lower; the sheet gives no 12 V curve, so it must be measured or taken from a curve at that voltage.
The torque doubles.
Only the holding torque changes.
questions.explanation: At speed the winding current cannot rise as fast from a lower supply, so the torque falls. The SY42STH38 sheet gives only a 24 V, 1.68 A, half-step curve.

questions.prompt: A wheel drive needs more tractive force than mu x share x m g cos(slope). What happens, and what helps?
options: Nothing: a bigger motor always gives more force.
The wheels slip; more grip or more weight on the driven wheels helps, not a bigger motor.
The motor stalls and the driver current drops.
The battery voltage rises.
questions.explanation: The ground limits the force to mu N. Beyond that the wheels spin whatever the motor can deliver; the fix is grip, weight on the driven wheels or a gentler ramp.

questions.prompt: Write a test plan for functions trapezoid(distance, v_max, a_max) and rms(segments) used in a motor-sizing calculator.
rubric: Hand-computes one trapezoid case (for example 0.8 m, 0.5 m/s, 1.0 m/s^2 gives 2.1 s) and one triangle case, and checks the boundary where v_max^2 / a_max equals the distance.
Tests rms on a constant torque (RMS equals the value) and on a cycle with rest, and checks that adding rest time lowers the RMS.
Considers invalid inputs: zero or negative acceleration, zero distance, an empty list of segments.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Size a vertical Z axis for a 3 kg carriage on a stepper-driven 8 mm lead screw: list the numbers you need, the formulas, and the checks that could fail.
rubric: Computes thrust m g plus acceleration, the screw efficiency from lead, mean diameter and friction (or takes it from a source), the motor torque F l / (2 pi eta), and applies the stepper safety factor once.
Compares the required torque with the pull-out curve at the needed pulse rate and at the supply voltage the curve was measured at, and checks the winding temperature or duty.
Checks whether the screw is self-locking and plans a brake, counterweight or spring if not; checks the driver current limit, voltage and cooling.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
